patterns.what_worked: Pinning the gather against the REAL compat probe (not a stubbed api table) caught the one real trap in the spec: compat reads the client's INVSLOT_* range through rawget(_G, ...) at CALL time, so a fixture that only stubs the env globals answers 'unknown' forever. The mutation proofs then earned their keep - mutant B (a re-added TBC SHIFT hold) was killed by BOTH the behavioural pin and a static 'named in a comment, never in code' scan.
patterns.what_was_hard: The spec's literal `api.is_item_equipped(8345) or nil` would have collapsed the proven FALSE into nil (false or nil is nil in Lua) - the operator's brief said keep the tri-state, so the spec text was not copied literally; that divergence is recorded in the bench artifact. Also kept an eye on a concurrent lane (hunter-serpent) writing classes/hunter.lua in the same tree, which made the whole-tree luacheck warning count flicker.
patterns.skill_gap: Reading a spec's code-shaped instruction literally and shipping it without checking the three-value semantics of `and/or` - a habit worth breaking at the review step, not after the mutation proofs.
